name: Chat Room
description: A single shared chat room with live message delivery and typing indicators
backend_requirements: Access control: anyone may read the message history and listen on the WebSocket; require auth for sending messages and typing notices; admin endpoints are restricted to the admin account
Messages: text is a required non-empty string of at most 1000 characters after trimming; each message carries the username of the signed-in user who sent it
Messages are stored durably (they survive a restart) and are never edited
POST /api/messages stores a message and broadcasts it to every connected WebSocket client

GET /api/messages returns the most recent active messages in ascending id order; ?limit= sets how many (default 50, at most 100), ?before= returns only messages with an id below the given id (to load older history), and total counts every active message

WebSocket /api/ws/chat: clients connect with an optional ?token= carrying their sign-in token; every client receives message frames {"type": "message", id, username, text, created_at} for each new message

Signed-in WebSocket clients may send {"type": "message", "text": ...}, which is stored and broadcast exactly like POST /api/messages, and {"type": "typing"}, which is broadcast to the other clients as {"type": "typing", "username": ...} and not stored

A frame the server cannot accept (no or invalid token, empty or too long text, unknown type) is answered with {"type": "error", "detail": "<message>"} to that client only, and the connection stays open
Deactivated messages (is_active false) are left out of GET /api/messages; the admin overview still lists them
Errors answer with a JSON object {"detail": "<message>"}: 400 for invalid input, 401 without a valid token, 403 for a non-admin on admin endpoints, 404 for unknown ids
frontend_requirements: Everyone sees the live message list read-only; signed-in users also get the message input with a send button, and visitors see a 'Sign in to chat' prompt in its place
Sign-in and registration forms that call /api/auth/login and /api/auth/register; keep the token for later requests and the WebSocket, show the signed-in username and offer sign-out

Message list showing username, text and time, the user's own messages styled differently; it loads history from /api/messages, appends live messages and scrolls to the newest unless the reader has scrolled up
A 'Load older messages' control that fetches earlier history with ?before=
The WebSocket connection reconnects automatically with an increasing delay and shows a connection status (connected, reconnecting)
While a signed-in user types, send a typing notice at most every 2 seconds; show '<username> is typing...' for other users and hide it 3 seconds after their last notice
admin_requirements: Admin overview: every message, active or not, with total, active and inactive counts
Toggle a message's active status from the overview to hide or restore it
